correctness.rationale: The general extremality premise is explicitly proved in Kosche–Koß–Manea–Siemer Proposition 3.14 and is restated/generalized in the later Adamson et al. work. For the extremal word itself, the new proof is self-contained: greedy matching advances one block exactly on the weak-zigzag inequalities, so an input of length k+1 is absent exactly when every transition advances. The parity reflection y_i=x_i for even i and y_i=sigma-1-x_i for odd i converts all zigzag inequalities to threshold-graph adjacencies. The packaged verifier independently confirms direct subsequence enumeration against this pattern, threshold-graph dynamic programming against reverse-accumulation, and exhaustive small-word bounds.

originality.rationale: The 2022 source proves the extremal construction but Proposition 3.10 provides only a non-tight exponential lower estimate and explicitly says that more careful analysis should improve it. It gives endpoint recurrences but does not identify or evaluate the exact general-alphabet maximum. The 2024 source supplies tight structural extremizers for arbitrary absent lengths but states that a closed form is provided for the opposite bound, not this maximal-absence count. Exact sequence, threshold-graph, characteristic-row, and alias searches found no published identification of the shortest-absent maximum with A050447.

value.rationale: The exact maximum number of shortest absent subsequences is a natural extremal invariant already singled out by the source. The source proves the maximizing family but leaves its own counting estimate explicitly non-tight. The result closes that quantitative gap for every alphabet size and universality index, gives a transparent weak-zigzag description of every extremal shortest absent subsequence, and connects the extremum to a classical threshold-graph walk array with immediate linear recurrences and generating functions.
